rounds.proof_sketch: ModelNew uses InstanceNorm2dCustom with default affine=True, creating weight and bias Parameters. CUDA dispatch checks `weight.defined() && bias.defined()` which is always true, routing to instance_norm_forward_kernel_with_affine. The mutation in instance_norm_forward_kernel (non-affine) is never executed.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation modifies the loop condition in `instance_norm_forward_kernel`, but this kernel is only called when affine=False. The ModelNew class instantiates InstanceNorm2dCustom with default affine=True, which creates weight and bias as nn.Parameter tensors. These tensors are always defined, so the CUDA dispatch condition `weight.defined() && bias.defined()` is always true, causing the code to always execute `instance_norm_forward_kernel_with_affine` instead. The mutated kernel is dead code under this fixed model configuration, explaining the bitwise equivalence observed in Layer 2 across all 112 test rounds.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed contract. The mutation is in a non-affine kernel that is never called because the model always uses affine=True. Changing this would require modifying the model configuration, which is not allowed under the testing contract.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing frameworks should identify mutations in code paths that are unreachable under the fixed test configuration and mark them as equivalent mutations. Additionally, parameterized testing that varies model constructor arguments (not just input values) would be needed to kill mutations in conditional code paths.
